semantic_correction.stem: A hospitalized client suddenly develops facial droop, arm weakness, and aphasia. The nurse activates the facility stroke alert. What is the main purpose of this activation?

options.A: Mobilize the stroke team for rapid assessment, imaging, and time-sensitive treatment decisions while stroke is still suspected.
options.B: Wait for imaging to confirm stroke before involving the stroke team or beginning the coordinated response.
options.C: Complete laboratory testing and specialty consultations before brain imaging so the diagnostic workup is finished first.
options.D: Replace bedside neurologic assessment because the stroke team will evaluate the client's deficits later.

semantic_correction.rationale: The 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guideline emphasizes expeditious evaluation and treatment, organized stroke protocols, and immediate availability of a stroke team because treatment benefit is highly time dependent. A stroke alert is therefore used to mobilize a coordinated response when acute stroke is suspected so assessment, brain imaging, and treatment decisions occur without avoidable delay. Definitive diagnosis is not required before the emergency pathway begins, and activation does not replace ongoing bedside neurologic assessment.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Activate the stroke response promptly when acute focal neurologic deficits are recognized so coordinated assessment, imaging, and treatment decisions begin without avoidable delay.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed 'all'/'only' distractor cueing, shortened the correct answer, and centered the item on the time-sensitive systems purpose of stroke-alert activation before definitive diagnosis.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original answer was uniquely longest and distractors used absolutes. The revised item directly tests early coordinated stroke-system activation with balanced alternatives.

option_audit.A: Correct. It captures the purpose of rapid stroke-system activation while the diagnosis is still being established.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Requiring imaging confirmation before team activation introduces avoidable delay.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Exhaustive testing before imaging/treatment decisions conflicts with the guideline's emphasis on expeditious evaluation.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Stroke-team activation complements rather than replaces bedside neurologic assessment.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone reflects the purpose and timing of the coordinated stroke response.
cueing_check: All four options are descriptions of stroke-alert function of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
